original_question: (M. Bridson). Let Fm be a free group of rank m and let ϕ ∈ Aut(Fm) be a polynomially growing automorphism of maximal degree m − 1, which means that for some(equivalently, any) free basis {x1,..., xm } of Fm, the sequence maxi |ϕn(xi)| grows at the rate of nm−1, where |g| denotes the minimal length of g in the xi and their inverses. a) Is the free-by-cyclic group Fm ⋊ϕ Z virtually special? b) In particular, are the Hydra groups Gm = Fm ⋊ Z = ⟨a1,..., am, t | t−1 a1 t = a1, t−1 ai t = ai ai−1 for all i > 1⟩ virtually special?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.125 (M. Bridson) in Section 21, “New Problems,” of the 21st issue of The Kourovka Notebook. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it correctly identifies the ambient group F_m, the hypothesis that φ ∈ Aut(F_m) is polynomially growing of maximal degree m−1, the basis-independent growth condition max_i |φ^n(x_i)| growing like n^{m−1}, the free-by-cyclic group F_m ⋊_φ Z, and the specific Hydra-group special case G_m with presentation t^{−1}a_1t=a_1 and t^{−1}a_it=a_ia_{i−1} for i>1. In substance, it is essentially a transcription of Problem 21.125. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone in the paper’s sense, the term “virtually special” should be defined using the immediately preceding Problem 21.124: a group G is virtually special if it has a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a special complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The semidirect-product notation F_m ⋊_φ Z should explicitly say that a generator of Z acts on F_m by φ. This is implicit in the paper’s notation and in the Hydra presentation. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
Part (b) should be presented as the paper presents it: an “In particular” special case of part (a), not as an unrelated second question. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

If every quantifier is to be made explicit, one may state that m is a positive integer and rewrite “for all i > 1” as “for 2 ≤ i ≤ m”; these are implicit in the paper’s wording. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper does not further formalize the asymptotic phrase “grows at the rate of n^{m−1},” so a faithful refinement should keep that wording rather than replace it with a broader or stronger asymptotic convention not stated there. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let m ≥ 1, let F_m be the free group of rank m, and let φ ∈ Aut(F_m) be a polynomially growing automorphism of maximal degree m−1, meaning that for some (equivalently, any) free basis {x_1, ..., x_m} of F_m, the sequence max_i |φ^n(x_i)| grows at the rate of n^{m−1}, where |g| denotes the minimal word length of g in the letters x_1^{±1}, ..., x_m^{±1}. If F_m ⋊_φ Z denotes the semidirect product in which a generator of Z acts on F_m by φ, is F_m ⋊_φ Z virtually special, i.e. does it have a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a special complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise? In particular, does this hold for the Hydra groups G_m = ⟨a_1, ..., a_m, t | t^{−1}a_1t = a_1, t^{−1}a_it = a_ia_{i−1} for 2 ≤ i ≤ m⟩? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is already essentially the paper’s official problem statement. The only nearby context needed to make it genuinely self-contained is the definition of “virtually special,” which appears immediately before, in Problem 21.124. Because this source is a problem list rather than a theorem/proposition article, there is no narrower official reformulation to prefer over Problem 21.125 itself. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
